gateway_note: Buenos Aires: EZE for most international arrivals; AEP for many domestic sectors
seasonality_note: Summer suits Patagonian lakes, mountains and glaciers; winter suits the north and snow sports; spring and autumn work well for Buenos Aires, Iguazú and central routes.
operational_note: Suggested days and route intensity are VisaAdvisor editorial judgments.

gateway_note: Santa Cruz: VVI; La Paz/El Alto: LPB for an Andes-first route
seasonality_note: The official general planning window is the drier April-October period, but conditions differ between the high-altitude Andes and the tropical lowlands.
signature_experience_1_editorial: Salar de Uyuni and coloured lagoons
operational_note: Suggested days and route intensity are VisaAdvisor editorial judgments.

seasonality_note: There is no single national season. The Amazon is hot and humid year-round; the northeast coast is warm most of the year; May-September is a strong official window for Pantanal wildlife; the south is cooler in winter.
operational_note: A first trip should normally select two or three regions rather than attempt national coverage.

seasonality_note: Timing is regional: April-June is an official sweet spot for San Pedro de Atacama; December-March usually gives longer days for Patagonia and the Carretera Austral.
operational_note: Suggested days and route intensity are VisaAdvisor editorial judgments.

seasonality_note: December-March and July-August are often drier in major Andean and Caribbean routes. The Pacific is wet year-round; Amazon conditions change between higher-water and relatively drier periods.
operational_note: Seasonality must be checked against the selected region rather than treated as a national guarantee.

gateway_note: Quito: UIO; Guayaquil: GYE for some coast and Galapagos routes
seasonality_note: June-August is a strong Andean planning window. Galapagos works year-round: December-May is warmer, while June-November is cooler with different marine conditions.
operational_note: The 10-14-day suggestion assumes mainland Ecuador plus Galapagos; a mainland-only trip can be shorter.

gateway_note: Georgetown: GEO; OGL for many domestic connections
seasonality_note: Practical dry-season overlap is mid-January to early May and September to mid-November. Wet periods make roads harder but can strengthen waterfall and river experiences.
operational_note: Interior travel commonly uses a combination of small aircraft, boats, roads and licensed operators.

gateway_note: Asuncion: ASU; land borders carry most visitor arrivals
seasonality_note: Plan around heat tolerance and region: summer is commonly 25-35 C and can be hotter in the Chaco; winter is usually 10-20 C and may be cooler in the south.
operational_note: The gateway field notes the main airport but does not imply that most visitors arrive by air.

seasonality_note: Peru has no single season. April-October is the official recommended window for Cusco and Machu Picchu; the coast and Amazon follow different climate patterns.
signature_experience_1_editorial: Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley
operational_note: Suggested days allow Lima, Cusco and one additional region.

seasonality_note: February-April and mid-August-November are officially described as relatively drier windows. Rain can occur year-round and the timing of seasons can vary.
signature_experience_2_editorial: a river and rainforest journey into the interior
operational_note: Use licensed operators and describe Maroon and Indigenous communities with respect and context.

seasonality_note: December-February is the coastal summer peak; southern right whales are commonly promoted from July-October; grape harvest experiences concentrate in February-March.
signature_experience_2_editorial: Cabo Polonio and the Atlantic coast
operational_note: Montevideo and Colonia work year-round; the coast, whales and harvest are month-specific choices.

gateway_note: Caracas/Maiquetia: CCS is normally the main gateway; verify current operating airport before booking
seasonality_note: Canaima is generally drier January-March and wetter April-December; Los Roques is comparatively dry. Current transport operations override normal seasonal planning.
operational_note: State reporting checked 2 August cited NOTAM CO765/26 for a technical closure through 22 August and a provisional progressive commercial restart planned for 24 August. Recheck the airport and airline immediately before planning; the date is not a guarantee.
